BiblicalUsage: Long is used for time and for measure, and the Bible stretches it both ways. The war between the house of Saul and the house of David was long, Jeremiah tells the exiles their captivity will be long, and Zophar says God's measure is longer than the earth and broader than the sea.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe 'long' is honest about how God's work feels: wars drag on, exiles drag on, and God's measure is longer than anything we can pace out. And I hold that the length is not delay, it is God working at His own measure, which is longer than the earth and deeper than hell.
